reason: Conversation 1 asks sensible diagnostic questions, has the customer turn the drum by hand with the machine unplugged, and links the cold-morning pattern to a worn pulley while still allowing a belt as an alternative. It then takes the customer's back problem into account and recommends an engineer, which fits the expected escalation. It overstates the pulley as 'strongly' indicated and wrongly says it can't look up the model, but it never claims certainty. Conversation 2 is terse and repeats a generic coins-and-buttons check. It never suggests checking levelling or localising the noise, and it names the jockey pulley as the cause after only a superficial exchange. It also ignores the customer's earlier answers, and its closing engineer advice gives no reasoning and doesn't address the customer's physical limits or the alternative of worn drum rollers.
